name: blur-swap-link
title: Blur Swap Link
author: HoverUI (https://hoverui.com)
description: The label defocuses out as its replacement racks into focus. Whichever label is departing leads with its optics and whichever is arriving leads with its opacity, by 37.5% of the transition — that ordering, and the fact that it flips with the direction rather than being pinned to a span, is the whole difference between a rack focus and a crossfade with a blur bolted on. Both labels share one grid cell, so the box is the wider of the two and neither state can shift layout. Nothing ships to the client: it is a server component with no hooks and no handlers, and the whole effect is CSS. `children` is the real text and the accessible name; the `swap` label is hidden from assistive technology because the swap is decorative and the link's identity is the resting label regardless of which one is visible — note that keyboard users DO reach the swapped state, so a sighted keyboard user sees `swap` while the link announces `children`. It reads the hover and :focus-visible of an ancestor `a`, `button`, `[role=button]` or `summary` as well as its own, so wrapping it in your link works; any other wrapper (a `[role=link]`, a `<div tabindex="0">`) gets neither, and the component is inert inside one. Under reduced motion the swap still happens but the duration is zeroed, so the exchange is instant rather than animated. On touch and any device without hover it rests showing `children`, sharp and opaque.
